parts.title: Listening Passage 1
parts.transcriptHtml:
Officer: Good morning. Can I help you?

Student: Yes. I’ve just been accepted on a course at the university, and I’d like to try and arrange accommodation in the hall of residence.

Officer: Yes. Certainly. Please sit down. What I’ll do is fill in a form with you to find out a little more about your preferences and so forth.

Student: Thank you.

Officer: So first of all, can I take your name?

Student: It’s Anubhat.

Officer: Could you spell your name, please?

Student: Yes. A n u b h a, t t.

Officer: Thanks. And could I ask your date of birth?

Student: The 03/31/1972.

Officer: Thank you. And where are you from?

Student: India.

Officer: Oh, right. And, what will you be studying?

Student: I’m doing a course in nursing.

Officer: Right. Thank you. And how long would you want to stay in hall, do you think?

Student: Well, it would take three years, but I’d only like to stay in hall for two. I’d like to think about living outside for the third year.

Officer: Fine. And what did you have in mind for catering? Do you want to cook for yourself or have all your meals provided?

Student: That that’s full board. Is there something in between?

Officer: Yes. You can just have evening meal provided, which is half board.

Student: That’s what I’d prefer.

Officer: Yes. A lot of students opt for that. Now with that in mind, do you have any special diet? Anything we should know about?

Student: Yes. I don’t take red meat. No red meat.

Officer: Now thinking about the room itself, we have a number of options. You can have a single study bedroom, or you can have a shared one. These are both what we call simple rooms. The other alternative is to opt for a single bed sit, which actually has more space and better facilities. There’s about 20 a week difference between them.

Student: Well, actually, my grant is quite generous, and I think the bedsit sounds the best option.

Officer: Lovely. I’ll put you down for that, and we’ll see what availability is like. Now can I ask some other personal details which we like to have on record?

Student: Yes. Of course.

Officer: I wonder if you could let us know what your interests are. This might help us get a closer match for placing you in a particular hall.

Student: Well, I love the theater.

Officer: Right.

Student: And I enjoy sports, particularly badminton.

Officer: Ah, that’s worth knowing. Now what we finish with on the form is really a list from you of what your priorities are in choosing a hall, and we’ll do our best to take these into account.

Student: Well, the first thing is I’d prefer a hall where there are other mature students, if possible.

Officer: Yes. We do have halls which tend to cater for slightly older students.

Student: And I’d prefer to be out of town.

Officer: That’s actually very good for you because we tend to have more vacancies in out of town halls.

Student: Lucky. Yes.

Officer: Anything else?

Student: Well, I would like somewhere with a shared area, a a TV room, for example, or or something like that. It’s a good way to socialize.

Officer: Certainly is. That’s it? Now we just need a contact telephone number for you.

Student: Oh, sure. I’ll just find it. It’s 667549.

Officer: Great. So we’ll be in contact with you as soon as possible.

questionSets.instructionHtml: Complete the form below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

Accommodation Form – Student Information

Example: Type of accommodation: hall of residence
Name: Anu ______
Date of birth: ______ 1972
Country of origin: India
Course of study: ______
Number of years planned in hall: ______
Preferred catering arrangement: half board
Special dietary requirements: no ______ (red)
Preferred room type: a single ______
Interests:
  • the ______
  • badminton
Priorities in choice of hall:
  • to be with other students who are ______
  • to live outside the ______
  • to have a ______ area for socialising
Contact phone number: 667549
